title: The Night Garden Atlas
summary: On the night before her atlas goes on display, Inez follows an ivory moth through a rooftop garden. To draw its route, she has to reconsider the blue pin she placed beside a lighted window.
coverAlt: In an indigo cut-paper rooftop garden, a dark-curled child kneels beside an iron gate with an accordion notebook. An ivory moth with two dark wing spots rests on a large, pale moonflower.
style: Layered hand-cut paper and cyanotype botanical prints in indigo, black, and warm ivory, with two portrait panels on each landscape story page.

pages.alt: Inez kneels over an accordion-fold sketchbook on a rooftop ledge beside a blue pencil and pin. Under a canopy of leaves, she passes through an iron gate toward a lighted window.
pages.transcript:
Tomorrow her atlas would go in the library window.
Tonight Inez had one blank leaf left.

pages.alt: A pale spotted moth flies beside the lit potting-shed window. Seen from above, Inez kneels below the glass to follow its curved flight with her pencil.
pages.transcript:
The potting shed shone like a little square moon.
Under it, an ivory moth wrote circles in the dark.

pages.alt: Close up, Inez marks the window on her sketched city map. She holds the open book toward the real illuminated square, framed by dark vines.
pages.transcript:
Inez drew the square and pressed a blue pin beside it.
There. An address for a moth.

pages.alt: Inez crouches beneath a row of large moonflowers by the fence. An overhead view shows the moth looping back over the stone path while Inez looks up from her book.
pages.transcript:
White trumpets had opened all along the fence.
The moth passed them all and swung back to the glass.

pages.alt: Inez raises one hand beside her reflection as the moth clings to the bright pane. She crouches beneath it with her folded atlas resting on the ground.
pages.transcript:
Its feet ticked against the pane. Then again.
Inez shut her book. A circle could mean trouble.

pages.alt: Aunt Luz, with a silver bun and round glasses, works at the seed table inside. Outside, Inez lifts her dark-backed book toward a square of window light.
pages.transcript:
Inside, Aunt Luz tucked seeds into paper sleeves.
Inez held up her atlas. Its shadow fell across the pane.

pages.alt: Inez and Aunt Luz stand among moonflowers beside the shed and look up at the shutter. Luz swings its dark panel across the window as a narrow stripe of light falls across the ground.
pages.transcript:
“Aunt Luz, could we try the shutter?”
Luz swung it round. One thin stripe of light lay on the path.

pages.alt: The pale moth flies away from a narrow lit edge and into dark foliage. In a separate deep-blue pool of shadow, Inez sits still and peers up beneath the leaves.
pages.transcript:
The moth slipped past the stripe into the leaves.
Inez waited long enough for the dark to grow edges.

pages.alt: Inez peers between leaves at a luminous moonflower and the small moth hovering near it. The second panel moves close to the spotted moth on the flower’s broad, pale rim.
pages.transcript:
First she made out one pale trumpet at the wall.
Then she saw its visitor. Six small feet gripped the rim.

pages.alt: Extreme close-up shows the moth’s fine mouthpart uncurling against a petal. A cutaway of the long trumpet-shaped flower reveals the slender tongue reaching inside.
pages.transcript:
Under its chin, a tiny coil loosened.
A tongue as fine as thread reached down to the nectar.

pages.alt: Inez watches the dusted moth lift above one blossom. At a second moonflower the moth touches the center while her pencil sketches its visit in the foreground.
pages.transcript:
When the moth rose, pollen powdered its head.
At the next flower, a little of that dust rubbed off.

pages.alt: Inez looks across a narrow city alley toward a fire escape and its flower box as the moth crosses the gap. She stretches her small accordion atlas along the railing between the gardens.
pages.transcript:
Across the alley, another white flower leaned from a fire escape.
Inez had drawn both buildings. She had left out the journey.

pages.alt: A close view shows Inez pulling a pin from the window drawn in her notebook. Bent over the garden ledge, she rubs at the mark beside the moonflower vine.
pages.transcript:
She pulled the blue pin out of the shed on her map.
She rubbed away its dot. Blue dust clung to her thumb.

pages.alt: Inez unfolds the atlas across the ledge. A view over her shoulder shows a vine, fire-escape ladder, and flower box on separate panels, with a moth above them.
pages.transcript:
Three blank folds reached from elbow to elbow.
This time she drew a vine, a ladder, a box of flowers.

pages.alt: In morning light a younger child traces the atlas beside Inez at the library window. Inez’s hand lifts from the blank last fold, and beyond the window a pale moth rests under a leaf.
pages.transcript:
At the library, one small finger crossed the gap between the gardens.
Inez left the last fold empty for another night’s flight.
